name: DatasetRecord
title: Dataset Record
description: Write a read's rows into the table an object owns, replacing what the same document wrote last time rather than landing a second set beside it
whenToUse: Store the rows a read produced, where the object they belong to owns a table. Give it the rows, the object, and what they were read from, and it replaces everything that source wrote before: a document read again corrects its figures instead of doubling them, and a read that finds nothing removes what it found last time, so a figure since withdrawn stops being reported. Every column is checked against the object's own declaration, so a row carrying a name the table does not have is refused rather than dropped. It cannot create or alter a table.

inputs.name: rows
inputs.description: The rows to write, each a record whose keys are columns the object declares

outputs.name: removed
outputs.description: How many rows this replaced, so a read that found fewer than last time is visible

object.title: Object
object.description: Which object's table, by its name (the object must declare one in dataset.yaml)

org.title: Organisation
org.description: Whose rows these are. Set on every row and enforced by the database, never by the query

of.title: Of
of.description: The id of the row these belong to. Every row is deleted with it

document.title: Read from
document.description: The id of the document these were read from. What this source wrote before is replaced; leave it empty to replace everything this owner has.

rows.title: Rows
rows.description: The rows as a JSON array, or wired, e.g. return signal.readings

emitOnTestRun.title: Perform on test runs
emitOnTestRun.description: This step acts outside the platform and cannot be undone, so test runs trace it rather than perform it. Enable only while testing this step, then switch it off.

authRequired.title: Require sign-in
authRequired.description: Only a signed-in caller may run this step. Leave off and it runs for whoever the workflow's trigger admitted, which is the usual answer.

authRole.title: Require role
authRole.description: A claim the caller's account must carry, as noun:verb (finance:approve, payments:refund). Leave blank to require only that they are signed in.

package.name: dataset
package.packageFile:
# DATASET — the table an object owns (docs/unoverse/data/objects/dataset.md). An object that
# holds many small facts read together, rather than one row read alone, declares its columns and
# the platform makes it a real table: real types, real indexes, and access the database enforces.
#
# TWO DOORS, two nodes. Rows in (DatasetRecord), rows out (DatasetQuery). Neither can create or
# alter a table: structure changes only through a migration generated from the declaration and
# approved by a person, and the role this runs as has no permission to do otherwise.
#
# THE HOST IS THE ENGINE, at loopback, as the documents package explains: a node's call must be
# https or loopback, and the engine holds what the database's address is so no node and no file
# does.
name: dataset
displayName: Dataset
description: >-
  Put rows into the table an object owns, and read them back: filtered, limited, and summed only
  within one unit
version: 0.1.0
category: storage
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1751366180/gravity/icons/gravityIcon.png

features:
  - Write a read's rows, replacing what the same document wrote last time
  - Read rows back filtered by any declared column, by value, by list or by range
  - Sum and rank, always grouped by unit so unlike figures are never added together
  - Every column checked against the object's own declaration, so a name is never taken from a caller

allowedHosts:
  - 127.0.0.1

requires:
  executorVersion: ">=1.6.0"
  transport: [json]

files.api/events.yaml:
- emit: written
  value: "return (response || {}).written || 0"
- emit: removed
  value: "return (response || {}).removed || 0"
files.api/run.yaml:
- name: record
  method: POST
  url: "return scope.engineUrl + '/dataset/record'"
  transport: json
  body:
    object: "{{ config.object }}"
    org: "{{ config.org }}"
    of: "{{ config.of }}"
    document: "{{ config.document }}"
    rows: >-
      return (() => {
        const raw = config.rows;
        return Array.isArray(raw) ? raw : (String(raw || '').trim() ? JSON.parse(String(raw)) : []);
      })()
  timeoutMs: 60000
  error:
    when: "return !!response.error"
    message: "return response.error"
files.config.yaml:
configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [object, of, rows]
  properties:
    object:
      type: string
      title: Object
      description: Which object's table, by its name (the object must declare one in dataset.yaml)
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    org:
      type: string
      title: Organisation
      description: Whose rows these are. Set on every row and enforced by the database, never by the query
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    of:
      type: string
      title: Of
      description: The id of the row these belong to. Every row is deleted with it
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    document:
      type: string
      title: Read from
      description: >-
        The id of the document these were read from. What this source wrote before is replaced;
        leave it empty to replace everything this owner has.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    rows:
      type: string
      title: Rows
      description: The rows as a JSON array, or wired, e.g. return signal.readings
      default: "[]"
      "ui:field": template
"ui:order": [object, org, of, document, rows]
files.interface.yaml:
inputs:
  - name: rows
    type: array
    description: The rows to write, each a record whose keys are columns the object declares
    required: false

outputs:
  - name: written
    type: number
    description: How many rows were written
  - name: removed
    type: number
    description: How many rows this replaced, so a read that found fewer than last time is visible

credentials: []
files.node.yaml:
type: DatasetRecord
kind: PromiseNode

name: Dataset Record
category: Storage & Data
color: "#334155"
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1751366180/gravity/icons/gravityIcon.png

description: >-
  Write a read's rows into the table an object owns, replacing what the same document wrote last
  time rather than landing a second set beside it

whenToUse: >-
  Store the rows a read produced, where the object they belong to owns a table. Give it the rows,
  the object, and what they were read from, and it replaces everything that source wrote before:
  a document read again corrects its figures instead of doubling them, and a read that finds
  nothing removes what it found last time, so a figure since withdrawn stops being reported.
  Every column is checked against the object's own declaration, so a row carrying a name the
  table does not have is refused rather than dropped. It cannot create or alter a table.

auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # It changes what is stored, and a second identical call is not a second set of rows: it
  # replaces. Still not undoable by itself, so it is never treated as a pure read.
  emitsExternally: true
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
# SAMPLE DATA, so the node can be loaded and run from the Nodes screen. It writes two rows
# against an object that owns a table, for one owner, read from one document. Running it again
# writes two and removes two: the same source replaces itself rather than doubling.
testData:
  config:
    object: observation
    org: example
    of: row-1
    document: doc-1
    rows: >-
      [{"fund":"Example Fund","measure":"exposure","dimension":"sectors","label":"Alpha",
        "side":"long","value":"1.84","unit":"percent_of_aum","as_of":"2026-05-31",
        "scope":"whole","basis":"reported","source":"2. Exposure, row 5"},
       {"fund":"Example Fund","measure":"exposure","dimension":"sectors","label":"Alpha",
        "side":"short","value":"-0.40","unit":"percent_of_aum","as_of":"2026-05-31",
        "scope":"whole","basis":"reported","source":"2. Exposure, row 5"}]
  inputs:
    rows: []
  expect:
    written: "return output.written === 2"
    removed: "return typeof output.removed === 'number'"
